encounters.cc: 3-week history of a worsening scalp lesion

lines: 3-week history of a worsening scalp lesion
The patient is a 12-year-old male with longitudinal follow-up in pediatrics and psychiatry since 2020.
He presents to the dermatology clinic with his mother due to a 3-week history of a worsening scalp lesion.
The child complains of mild itching and occasional tenderness at the site.
His mother noticed a circular patch of hair loss with black dots and some scaling on the crown of his head.
He has no fever or systemic symptoms.
Active Problem List:
- Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
Home Medications:
- Methylphenidate 10 mg PO twice daily
NKDA
- Father: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder
- Maternal cousin: Learning disability
He attends daycare and recently adopted a stray kitten.
Physical examination reveals a 3-cm circular patch of alopecia with broken hairs, scaling, and minimal surrounding erythema.
A Wood lamp examination does not reveal fluorescence.
Potassium hydroxide (KOH) preparation of hair shafts shows segmented hyphae within hair shafts.
